title_ja: CFTCスタッフ書簡26-30 日次決済における信託会社利用
original_text:
Re: Request for No-Action Position Concerning Commission Regulation 39.14(c)
               and (d)

[Addressee withheld.]
This is in response to a letter from Nodal Clear, LLC (“Nodal”) dated October 29, 2026,
to the Division of Clearing and Risk (“Division”) of the Commodity Futures Trading
Commission (“Commission”). In the letter, Nodal requests that the Division issue a no-action
letter confirming that the Division will not recommend that the Commission commence
enforcement action against a derivatives clearing organization (“DCO”) for conducting daily
settlement with clearing members using a trust company, notwithstanding Commission
Regulation 39.14 defining “settlement bank,” in relevant part, as “a bank.”

Background and Statement of Facts

        Based on the representations made in the letter, the Division understands the relevant
facts to be as follows:

       The Commission’s customer protection framework is set forth in Section 4d of the
Commodity Exchange Act (the “Act”)1 and parts 1 and 22 of the Commission’s regulations.2
Throughout these provisions, the statute and regulations consistently require that customer funds
be held with a “bank or trust company.” Section 4d of the Act and the Commission’s
implementing regulations establish this requirement as part of the framework for safeguarding
money, securities, and other property deposited by customers. Specifically, the Commission
adopted Regulation 1.20 to implement Section 4d(a) of the Act, and part 22 to implement
Section 4d(f), establishing corresponding protections for futures customers and cleared swaps
customers, respectively.3


1
    7 U.S.C. § 6d.
2
    17 C.F.R. parts 1 and 22.
3
 See Enhancing Protections Afforded Customers and Customer Funds Held by Futures Commission Merchants and
Derivatives Clearing Organizations, 78 Fed. Reg. 68506 (Nov. 14, 2013).
 
[Addressee withheld.]
Page 2

       Nonetheless, Regulation 39.14, which sets forth requirements governing a DCO’s
settlement procedures, including the handling of funds belonging to clearing members and their
customers in connection with those procedures, defines a “settlement bank” in relevant part as “a
bank.”4 There are no references to trust companies in Regulation 39.14.

        Nodal represents that trust companies are subject to comprehensive state regulatory
oversight and supervision. For example, Nodal states that, in New York, the Department of
Financial Services applies the same level of scrutiny to banks and trust companies, and that both
banks and trust companies are chartered under the same provisions of New York banking law.
Nodal adds that the regulation and supervision of banks and trust companies is substantially
similar aside from the fact that trust companies, unlike banks, generally are not authorized to
offer consumer deposit accounts or to make loans and that, as a result, trust companies can have
different capital requirements than banks.

        Finally, Nodal represents that state-regulated trust companies are among the leading
custodians of digital assets. Nodal further states that clarifying that DCOs may use trust
companies to conduct daily settlements with clearing members will facilitate the ability of DCOs
to accept such assets as margin collateral by allowing them to seamlessly integrate such assets
into their existing daily workflows for collateral movement.

Discussion of Request for No-Action Position

        Nodal requests that the Division clarify that a DCO may use a trust company to conduct
daily settlements with clearing members in accordance with Regulation 39.14, notwithstanding
that Regulation 39.14 does not explicitly make reference to a trust company. In support, Nodal
points to the Commission’s customer protection requirements in Section 4d of the Act and part 1
of the Commission’s regulations, which require that customer funds be held with a bank or trust
company.

        Nodal argues that the customer protection benefits of using a trust company are
consistent with and equivalent to using a bank. Nodal notes that neither the Act nor Regulation
39.14 imposes any requirements directly on settlement banks, instead imposing requirements on
DCOs that address how DCOs conduct daily settlements and how they select and monitor their
settlement banks.5 Nodal states that the requirements that the Commission imposes on DCOs for
daily settlements can apply equally to daily settlements with trust companies. Nodal adds that a
DCO can use its existing procedures and criteria for evaluating and monitoring settlement banks
to ensure that the DCO complies with the requirements in Regulation 39.14(c) to evaluate and
monitor a trust company it uses for daily settlements with clearing members.

         Furthermore, Nodal notes that Regulation 39.14 has not been substantively revised since
it was adopted in 2011, and the derivatives markets have evolved significantly since then. As a
result, and given that a trust company is an acceptable depository under the Commission’s

4
    17 C.F.R. § 39.14(a)(2).
5
    See 7 U.S.C. § 7a-1(c)(2)(E) and 17 C.F.R. § 39.14.
 
[Addressee withheld.]
Page 3

customer protection framework, Nodal argues that a trust company should also be considered
acceptable to perform the daily settlement functions required by Regulation 39.14.

No-Action Position

        Based on the facts presented and the representations Nodal has made, the Division will
not recommend that the Commission take enforcement action against any DCO for using a trust
company to conduct daily settlements with clearing members, if the DCO treats the trust
company as if it were a settlement bank for the purpose of compliance with Regulations 39.14(c)
and (d).

         This letter, and the position taken herein, represent the views of the Division only, and do
not necessarily reflect the views of the Commission or any other division or office of the
Commission. This letter, and the no-action position taken herein, are not binding on the
Commission. Further, this letter, and the position taken herein, concern enforcement action only
and do not represent a legal conclusion with respect to the applicability of any provision of the
Act or the Commission’s regulations. Except as explicitly provided in this letter, the no-action
position taken in this letter does not excuse persons relying on it from compliance with any other
applicable requirements contained in the Act or the Commission’s regulations. Because this
position is based on the representations contained in Nodal’s request letter, any different,
changed, or omitted material facts or circumstances may require a different conclusion or render
this letter void. Finally, as with all no-action letters, the Division retains the authority to
condition further, modify, suspend, terminate, or otherwise restrict the terms of this letter, in
their discretion.


Sincerely,




_______________________________
Richard Haynes
Acting Director
Division of Clearing and Risk
translation_ja:
## PDF 1頁

CFTC書簡26-30、2026年11月5日、ノーアクション。委員会規則39.14(c)・(d)についての不執行見解の要請。宛名・連絡先は省略。

Nodal Clear, LLCの2026年10月29日付書簡に回答する。委員会規則39.14は決済銀行を「銀行」と定義しているが、Nodalは、デリバティブ清算機関が信託会社を通じて清算会員との日次決済を行っても、清算・リスク部門が委員会に執行措置を勧告しない旨の書簡を求めた。

背景と事実。要請書の説明に基づくと、顧客保護の枠組みは商品取引所法4d条と委員会規則第1・22部に置かれている。法令は顧客資金を銀行または信託会社に保管するよう一貫して求める。これは顧客が預けた金銭、有価証券、その他の財産を保護する制度の一部。規則1.20は先物顧客向けに4d(a)条を実施し、第22部は清算済みスワップ顧客向けに4d(f)条を実施する。脚注は米国法典第7編6d条、連邦規則集17編第1・22部、顧客保護を強化する2013年11月14日付官報78 FR 68506。

## PDF 2頁

一方、規則39.14は清算会員とその顧客の資金の取扱いなど、清算機関の決済手続を定め、決済銀行を「銀行」と定義する。同規則に信託会社への言及はない。

Nodalによれば、信託会社は州の包括的な規制・監督を受ける。例えばニューヨーク州の金融サービス局は銀行と信託会社を同じ水準で審査し、双方は同じ州銀行法の規定に基づいて免許を受ける。Nodalは、信託会社は一般に個人預金口座の提供や貸出を認められず、資本要件が異なり得る点を除き、規制・監督は概ね同じだと説明する。さらに、州規制の信託会社には主要なデジタル資産の保管業者が含まれるため、信託会社を日次決済に使えることを明確にすると、既存の担保移動の業務にデジタル資産を組み込みやすくなり、証拠金担保としての受入れを促進すると述べる。

要請の検討。Nodalは、規則39.14に信託会社の明文がなくても日次決済に使えることを明らかにするよう求めた。商品取引所法4d条と委員会規則第1部が顧客資金を銀行または信託会社に預けるよう求めることを根拠とした。Nodalは、顧客保護上の利点は銀行と同等と主張する。法および規則39.14は決済銀行に直接義務を課さず、日次決済の方法、決済銀行の選定・監視の義務を清算機関に課す。要件は信託会社を使った場合にも適用できるという。清算機関は決済銀行の既存の評価・監視手順と基準を使い、信託会社について規則39.14(c)を遵守できるとする。Nodalは、規則39.14が2011年の採用以来実質的に改正されておらず、市場は大きく変化したことも指摘する。脚注は連邦規則集17編39.14(a)(2)、米国法典第7編7a-1(c)(2)(E)、連邦規則集17編39.14。

## PDF 3頁

信託会社は顧客保護の枠組みで認められた預託先なので、規則39.14が求める日次決済も担えるとNodalは主張する。

不執行見解。提示された事実とNodalの説明に基づき、清算機関が規則39.14(c)・(d)への適合のため信託会社を決済銀行として扱う場合、清算会員との日次決済に信託会社を使っても部門は委員会に執行措置を勧告しない。

この書簡と見解は部門のものに限られ、委員会や他の部門・部署の見解を反映するとは限らず、委員会を拘束しない。執行に限った見解であり、法や規則の適用についての法的結論ではない。明示した範囲を除き、他の適用要件を免除するものではない。重要な事実や状況に相違・変更・欠落があれば、結論が変わるか、書簡が無効になる場合がある。部門は裁量で条件の追加、変更、停止、終了、その他の制限を行う権限を留保する。署名は清算・リスク部門の局長代行。
facts_ja: 清算・リスク部門は、規則39.14(c)・(d)に沿って信託会社を決済銀行と同様に扱う場合、日次決済への利用について執行措置を勧告しないと表明。委員会を拘束せず、デジタル資産に関する説明は申請者の見解。
missing_parts: 全3頁の本文・脚注を確認。宛名・住所と署名の氏名は日本語版では役職に置換または省略。
